key_insight: Encoding an entire conformational ensemble into one thermodynamically informed embedding improves cyclic-peptide property prediction over single-structure or sequence-only approaches.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests that molecular design pipelines should model structural flexibility explicitly when predicting properties of peptides and other conformationally dynamic molecules.
method: Encode each conformer with shared EGNN layers.
Pool conformer embeddings with a Set Attention Block to form one ensemble representation.
Pretrain with masked token recovery, noisy-coordinate reconstruction, and pairwise distance reconstruction.
evidence_signal: On CREMP-CycPeptMPDB, scratch training failed ($R^2=0.005$), while the pretrained model reached $R^2=0.477$ and Pearson $r=0.699$, and the hybrid BERT+EnsembleEGNN model improved to $R^2=0.538$ and $r=0.737$.
watch_item: The gains depend on ensemble-quality data and pretraining, so performance may drop when conformer sampling is sparse, noisy, or unavailable.
paper_title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
